tool.name: recommend_framework
tool.description:
Opinionated framework recommendation from Techimpossible.

Asks the qualifying questions a real cybersecurity consultant asks on a scope call: 6 high-level routing questions (sector, AI involvement, customer profile, customer geographies, regulated data in scope, deal driver, org stage) plus 24 Codex foundational controls (6 per inventory: people, vendors, AI, data).

Returns a Codex-grounded recommendation: per-inventory foundational readiness, per-control state with what each missing control blocks, a primary program (which may legitimately be 'build foundation first' via Cybersecurity Fundamentals), queued recommendations with sequencing rationale, and an honest 'what we did not recommend' section.

Start here if you don't know which framework you need or want Techimpossible's perspective. Call gap_assess directly if you already know your framework.

tool.name: gap_assess
tool.description:
Express-path gap assessment against a known target framework.

Pass the framework (soc2, iso27001, hipaa, iso42001), AI involvement (explicit), and answers to the 24 Codex foundational controls. Returns a Codex-grounded report: a 2-3 sentence framing of what the framework covers, foundational readiness per inventory and per control (with what each missing control blocks), the recommended starting point (which may be Cybersecurity Fundamentals first if foundational inventories are incomplete), an ISO 42001 stacking recommendation when AI is in product, and a scope-call brief.

Operational/advanced/expert tier gaps are intentionally not assessed by this tool — they require deep framework knowledge and live-stack inspection that belong on the scope call. The foundational tier is the substance.

If you don't yet know your framework — or want Techimpossible's perspective on which fits — call recommend_framework first.

_published_faq.name: How do I add mcp-techimpossible-public to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add mcp-techimpossible-public to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector.
